en: Now, therefore, we shall explain devotion. 1.
But she, in this [state], consists of supreme love. ||2||
And she is of the nature of nectar. ||3||
Having obtained which, a person becomes perfected, becomes immortal, and becomes satisfied. ||4||
Having attained which, one desires nothing, does not grieve, does not hate, does not take delight, and does not become enthusiastic. ||5||
Having known which, one becomes conceited on account of me, and one becomes delighted in oneself. ||6||
She does not desire [it], because its nature is cessation. ||7||
Cessation, however, is the relinquishing of worldly and Vedic activities. ||8||
In that [state], there is non-duality and indifference toward its opposites. ||9||
The abandonment of other bases is non-duality. ||10||
In both worldly affairs and the Vedas, it consists of acting in accordance with that [truth] and maintaining indifference toward what is contrary to it. ||11||
Let there be the preservation of the scriptures hereafter, through the strengthening of one's resolve. ||12||
Otherwise, there would be the fear of falling [from one's status]. ||13||
The world, too, continues its activities such as eating only until the maintenance of the body is accomplished. (14)
The characteristics of the *tallaka* are now described according to the various differences of opinion. ||15||
"Paffection for worship and other such acts," says Pārāśarya. (16)
Garga says [the rule applies] in stories and so forth. ||17||
"Without contradicting one's delight in the Self," says Śāṇḍilya. (18)
Nārada, however, had entrusted all his conduct to her, and he was extremely distressed whenever he forgot her. ||19||
It is exactly so. ||20||
Just as in the case of the cowherd women of Vraja. ||21||
Even in that case, there is no denial of the greatness of his knowledge. ||22||
Devoid of that, it is like [the state] of paramours. ||23||
In that case, there is simply no such thing as being made happy by that happiness. ||24||
But that [devotion] is indeed superior even to the yoga of action and the yoga of knowledge. ||25||
Because it has the nature of a fruit. ||26||
Because even Īśvara possesses pride and aversion, and because he is fond of wretchedness. ||27||
Some maintain that knowledge alone is the means for that [liberation]. ||28||
Others say that there is mutual dependence. ||29||
Brahmakumāra says that it is itself of the nature of the fruit. ||30||
Because it is observed to be exactly so in cases such as the meal at Rājagṛha. ||31||
By that, there is neither satisfaction for the king nor the alleviation of hunger. ||32||
Therefore, that alone should be accepted by those seeking liberation. ||33||
The teachers sing its means of accomplishment. ||34||
But that [cessation] occurs through the abandonment of objects and the abandonment of attachment. ||35||
Because of the non-exclusion of devotion. ||36||
In this world as well, [this occurs] from hearing and chanting the qualities of the Blessed One. ||37||
But primarily, it is through great compassion alone, or by a mere fraction of the Lord’s grace. ||38||
But association with the great is rare, difficult to attain, and never in vain. ||39||
It is obtained only through his very grace. ||40||
Because there is no difference with respect to that person in that [state]. ||41||
Let that very thing be proven; let that very thing be proven! ||42||
Bad association must be abandoned in every way. ||43||
Because it is the cause of desire, anger, delusion, loss of memory, destruction of discernment, and total ruin. ||44||
Even these, though they have become like waves, become like the ocean through their association. ||45||
Who overcomes suffering? Who overcomes illusion? He who abandons attachment, he who serves those of great spiritual power, and he who becomes free from the sense of "mine.
He who resorts to a secluded place, who uproots the bond with the world, who becomes free from the three qualities, and who renounces acquisition and preservation; ||47||
He who renounces the fruit of action and relinquishes actions thereby becomes free from the pairs of opposites. ||48||
He who renounces even the Vedas attains nothing but uninterrupted devotion. ||49||
He crosses over; he crosses over; he causes the worlds to cross over. ||50||
The nature of love is indefinable. ||51||
Like one who tastes [something] while mute. ||52||
It reveals itself in some worthy recipient. ||53||
It is devoid of qualities, free from desire, increasing at every moment, uninterrupted, most subtle, and of the nature of direct experience. ||54||
Having attained that, one perceives only that, hears only that, speaks only that, and thinks only that. ||55||
The secondary [metaphorical] function is threefold, either due to the distinction of qualities (*guṇa*) or due to the distinction of the types such as the distressed (*ārta*). ||56||
Each preceding one is superior to each succeeding one. ||57||
From another [perspective], there is ease in devotion. ||58||
Because it does not depend on another means of valid cognition and is itself a means of valid cognition. ||59||
From that which has the form of peace and the form of supreme bliss. ||60||
No concern should be felt regarding the loss of the world, because it has been declared that one's own self and the Veda are the world. ||61||
Once that [realization] is established, worldly convention is not to be abandoned; rather, one must simply relinquish the fruit while continuing to perform its means. ||62||
One should not listen to accounts concerning women's wealth, nihilists, or the conduct of enemies. ||63||
Arrogance, hypocrisy, and the like should be abandoned. ||64||
Having surrendered all one's conduct to Him, one should direct desire, anger, pride, and so forth toward Him alone. 65.

Preceded by the destruction of the three-fold form [of worldly attachment], love consisting of eternal servitude and the worship of the Eternal Beloved must be cultivated; indeed, love alone is what must be cultivated. //66//
The principal devotees are those who are single-mindedly devoted. ||67||
Conversing with one another through choked throats, horripilation, and tears, they sanctify their families and the earth. ||68||
They make holy places into true pilgrimage sites, they make actions into virtuous deeds, and they make scriptures into true sacred texts. ||69||
They consist of that. ||70||
The ancestors rejoice, the deities dance, and this earth becomes possessed of its protector. ||71||
Among them, there is no distinction based on birth, learning, appearance, lineage, wealth, ritual action, or the like. ||72||
Because they belong to him. ||73||
One should not rely on debate. ||74||
Because of its abundance, its scope, and its lack of restriction. ||75||
The scriptures on devotion are to be contemplated, and the actions that bring about that understanding are to be performed. ||76||
When one awaits the time when pleasure, pain, desire, and gain have ceased, not even half a moment should be spent in vain. //77//
Virtues such as non-violence, truthfulness, purity, compassion, and faith must be maintained. ||78||
At all times and with one's whole being, the Blessed One alone should be worshipped by those free from anxiety. ||79||
When being glorified, he quickly manifests himself and causes his devotees to experience [his presence]. ||80||
Devotion alone to the Triple Truth is most excellent; devotion alone is most excellent. ||81||

Although it is of a single nature consisting of attachment to the greatness of qualities, attachment to the form, attachment to worship, attachment to remembrance, attachment to servitude, attachment to friendship, attachment to parental affection, attachment to the beloved, attachment to self-surrender, attachment to being absorbed in Him, and attachment to supreme separation, it becomes elevenfold. ||82||

Thus speak the teachers of devotion—Kumāra, Vyāsa, Śuka, Śāṇḍilya, Garga, Viṣṇu, Kauṇḍilya, Ceṣa, Uddhava, Aruṇi, Bala, Hanūmat, Vibhīṣaṇa, and others—who are of one mind and fearless of public gossip. ||83||
Whoever has faith in and believes this instruction of Śiva proclaimed by Nārada becomes possessed of devotion; he attains the Beloved; he attains the Beloved. Thus [ends the chapter]. 84.
